chunks: I advise you, O creatures of Allah, to detach from this world.
Which is leaving you even if you do not like its departure, and aging your bodies even if you like to renew them,
For your example and its example is like a journey where they traveled a path as if they had crossed it, and aimed at a landmark as if they had reached it,
How short is the distance for the runner to the goal to run towards it until he reaches it!
And how short is the stay of one who has a day he cannot exceed, while a swift driver is driving him in this world until he departs from it!

key_terms.الْمُبْلِيَةِ: The aging / causing to grow old
key_terms.يَوْمٌ: A day (referring to a limited lifespan)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the transient nature of the world in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of a traveler who has already reached their destination to illustrate the transient nature of worldly life, urging believers to detach despite their natural attachment. This rhetorical device underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as rejection of the world, but as recognizing its temporary status relative to the eternal hereafter. The exhortation serves as a spiritual reminder that death is the inevitable horizon for all, regardless of one's haste or desire for permanence.
